tagline: The open-source scheduling leader owns its niche in AI answers — but loses the generic buyer questions to Calendly almost every time.
summary: Cal.com has carved out total ownership of one AI-answer niche: any question containing 'open source' or 'self-hosted' scheduling returns Cal.com first, nearly every time. But the money is in the generic questions — 'best scheduling tool', 'best Calendly alternative' — and there, AI engines describe Cal.com through Calendly's frame ('an alternative to...') or omit it behind Acuity, Zoho Bookings and SavvyCal. The site is AI-readable (llms.txt present, 2,200+ extractable words) yet ships zero schema.org structured data, so engines get no machine-readable facts about pricing, product, or company to quote. The gap between niche dominance and generic invisibility is the whole opportunity.

money_queries.evidence: Answer-layer sources lead with Calendly and Zoho Bookings; Cal.com appears mid-list, framed as 'the open-source option'.
Consistently in the top 3 across the roundups engines retrieve (Zoho, Zeeg, calendly-alternatives.org), usually flagged for the generous free plan.
Owns this query outright — first answer in effectively every sampled source.
API-first positioning lands; cited alongside Nylas in developer-focused sources.

money_queries.query: best appointment booking app for small business
money_queries.evidence: SMB-service roundups (salons, clinics, coaches) go to Acuity, Square Appointments, Zoho — Cal.com unnamed in sampled sources.
Cal.com's unlimited free tier is its strongest fact, but answers default to Calendly's brand gravity; the free plan is mentioned when Cal.com appears at all.
Comparison content exists (G2, StackShare) but is authored on neutral/rival turf; G2's verdict language favors Calendly on satisfaction.
Cal.com's Stripe integration surfaces inconsistently; payment-scheduling answers split between Calendly, Acuity and SavvyCal.

sources.detail: Present in nearly every 'Calendly alternatives' listicle that answer engines retrieve — this is Cal.com's strongest citation asset.
Praised in r/selfhosted and dev threads, but generic scheduling advice threads default to Calendly; little Cal.com presence where non-developers ask.
No substantial standalone article — engines can't pull neutral encyclopedic facts about the company.
Listed with a review base far smaller than Calendly's; G2's comparative language positions Calendly as the default winner.
Setup tutorials exist; almost no third-party 'best scheduling tool' videos feature Cal.com prominently.
llms.txt present, docs and homepage are text-rich and crawlable — the site itself is a good citation source when engines find it.

roadmap.title: Ship schema.org JSON-LD sitewide
roadmap.why: The probe found zero structured data. Organization, SoftwareApplication and Offer markup (with the unlimited-free-plan priced at $0) hands engines quotable facts — the cheapest fix with the widest reach.

roadmap.title: Publish own-domain comparison pages for every rival
roadmap.why: 'Cal.com vs Calendly' answers are currently assembled from G2 and StackShare — turf that favors the incumbent. Honest, spec-level comparison pages on cal.com give engines a first-party source to cite.

roadmap.title: Target SMB-vertical queries where Cal.com is absent
roadmap.why: Booking-for-salons/clinics/coaches answers name Acuity and Square, never Cal.com. Vertical landing pages + presence in vertical roundups opens a market currently at 0% share of voice.

roadmap.title: Seed the 'free scheduling app' claim everywhere
roadmap.why: 'Unlimited free events' is a category-best fact that engines under-report. Get it into the roundups, review-site listings and Reddit threads engines actually quote.

roadmap.title: Build the Wikipedia-grade citation base
roadmap.why: Engines lean on encyclopedic sources for company facts. Press coverage and a properly sourced article give answers a neutral anchor Calendly already enjoys.

methodology_notes: Site AI-readiness measured by EchoRank's automated probe of cal.com on 2026-08-08 (llms.txt, robots.txt AI-crawler policy, schema.org JSON-LD, sitemap, extractable text).

AI-answer presence assessed by sampling the retrieval layer answer engines cite for each money query — the top-ranked comparison and roundup sources, review sites, and community threads — in August 2026.
Beta disclosure: results are a point-in-time sample of the public citation layer, not a paid API sweep of every engine; AI answers vary by user, session and engine version.
